newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo says dual AIDS drugs cut deaths.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo says dual AIDS drugs cut deaths.

text.p: Dual combination therapy using Glaxo-Wellcome's Epivir (3TC) and Retrovir (AZT) drugs cuts deaths from AIDS by more than 50 percent, the British company announced on Monday.

Data from the CAESAR trial of nearly 1,900 patients in 14 countries showed the best results yet from this class of drug, known as nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, the company told 1,700 delegates attending the Third International Congress on Drug Therapy in HIV Infection.
Epivir plus AZT reduced the progression of HIV infection to full-blown AIDS or death by 54 percent, and to death alone by 53 percent.

"The results confirm that 3TC/AZT is a cornerstone of our current treatment options and is helping our patients remain free of AIDS and live for longer," said Dr Brian Gazzard, an AIDS specialist at London's Chelsea and Westminster Hospital.

Doctors have been finding that combined drug therapy works much better than one drug alone against AIDS. The latest research says adding a new class of drugs, known as protease inhibitors, has even more dramatic effects.
The CAESAR trial, named after participant countries (Canada, Australia, Europe, South Africa), did not include protease inhibitors.
AIDS drugs tackle the HIV virus at various stages of its replicative cycle. Reverse transcriptase inhibitors stop an enzyme vital to the virus's invasion of an immune system cell.
